solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Desire is seen in women's hearts

indicators.note: the word is is spotted sitting inside the other two letters

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
H is the abbreviation for the card suit hearts

explanation.surface: A romantic claim that longing lies deep in women's hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'women's hearts' looks like one phrase meaning their centres, but it is two abbreviations, W and H, with IS placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a longing or want for something.

clue.text: Surprised exclamation about blight in wood

indicators.note: the exclamation goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: wow is what one says when amazed
an ill is a trouble or affliction, a blight

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at disease spreading through a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow is a type of tree and its timber, used for cricket bats, so an example of wood.

clue.text: Work with needle, taking a long time, and waste material

parts.note: to sew is to work with a needle and thread
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A slow needlework session followed by clearing away the scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is the waste matter carried off in drains and sewers.

clue.text: Former schoolfellows no longer ill? That's not made clear

parts.note: OBs are old boys, men who once attended a school
someone cured has recovered from illness

explanation.surface: Old school friends now recovered, though the point of the remark is left vague.
explanation.walkthrough: OB (old boy) is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured is hidden or made vague, so not rendered clear.

clue.text: Greeting first parts of body of work

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: An author opens a book with a salutation at the start of the main text.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow, bending from the waist, is a gesture of greeting or respect.

clue.text: Machine in the wings is the first thing seen in theatre

definitions.meaning: a literal reading: a device offstage that lifts the stage curtain

definitions.text: the first thing seen in theatre
definitions.meaning: a short opening play performed before the main piece

explanation.surface: Backstage machinery and what an audience sees first in a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a brief play put on before the main drama, and by extension any opening event.

clue.text: Shelter sports official, very large for a Cockney

parts.note: a ref is a referee

indicators.note: Cockneys drop the initial h sound, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: huge means very large

explanation.surface: A huge referee seeks cover, described in London dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, famous for dropping H at the start of words, turning HUGE into UGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of safety or protection, a synonym for shelter.

clue.text: Busy person ruined Monday

indicators.note: the word Monday is wrecked and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: An energetic worker has had the start of the week spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is figuratively a tireless, energetic person, named after the electrical generator.

clue.text: One's work on plot includes a clash of blades

definitions.text: One's work on plot includes a clash of blades

parts.words: One's work on plot includes a clash of blades
parts.note: sounds like a swordfight in a story's plot, but the plot is a garden plot and the blades are grass and the machine's cutters

explanation.surface: A novelist's storyline features a sword duel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' and 'blades' both read as story and swords; they are a patch of garden and grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden machine with rotating blades that cuts grass on a lawn.

clue.text: Maltreat new worker interrupting bloke

indicators.note: the new worker breaks into the middle of the word for a bloke

parts.note: a bloke is a man, a male
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A recruit cuts into a man's work and is treated roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle is to handle someone roughly, a close synonym for treating badly.

clue.text: Amount of money curtailed enjoyment

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a fund is a sum of money set aside

explanation.surface: Cutting a budget spoils the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun is amusement or pleasure, a synonym for enjoyment.

clue.text: No rag, badly edited, may be considered a newspaper

indicators.note: the letters of the words no rag are poorly put together, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A paper insists it is no tabloid, despite its sloppy editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' is slang for a poor newspaper, which fits the surface, but here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a periodical that speaks for a party or group, hence a newspaper.

clue.text: Line in magazine included in a morning mix

indicators.note: the magazine piece sits between the letter a and the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the magazine word

explanation.surface: A line of text appears in a magazine as part of a morning medley.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or combination, so a mix.

clue.text: Weapon taking top off simple cart

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a barrow is a basic hand cart

explanation.surface: A weapon made by removing the top of a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a projectile shot from a bow, a weapon.

clue.text: Necessitate angry speech after conflict

indicators.note: the angry speech comes after the conflict word in the answer

parts.note: war is armed conflict
a rant is a loud, angry tirade

explanation.surface: Fury in speeches following a war seems inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant is to justify or call for, so to make necessary.

clue.text: Friendly call receiving reduced attention

indicators.note: the call word takes the other piece into itself

parts.note: a cry is a shout or call

indicators.note: shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: heed means notice or attention

explanation.surface: A warm greeting gets less notice than it deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheery means cheerful and genial, close to friendly in manner.

clue.text: Speak about idiot making sense

indicators.note: the speaking word goes around the fool

parts.note: to say is to speak
nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Talking about a fool makes a sensible point.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is soundness of mind or reason, sense.

clue.text: Mountainous country — I make a mistake entering it

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the letters for it

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for 'it'
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A traveller admits to an error crossing a hilly land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mountainous country' tempts towards a nation name; it means rugged terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a range of jagged mountains, or a region of such peaks.

clue.text: Information collected by a heartless county organisation

indicators.note: the information comes right after the letter a, which picks it up

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the middle letters are removed, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: A shire with no heart gathers data for an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a business or body providing a service, an organisation.

clue.text: Difficult bottling oxygen for store

indicators.note: the difficult word holds the other letter inside, as a bottle holds gas

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: It is hard work keeping oxygen in a stockroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile kept hidden, and to hoard is to store up.

clue.text: Marine activity not quite sound in part of aircraft

indicators.note: the shortened healthy word is placed inside the aircraft part

parts.note: a wing is a part of a plane

indicators.note: the last letter is removed, so not the whole word

parts.note: sound in health, hale

explanation.surface: A noise from an aircraft's wing suggests something going on at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise from the aircraft, but here it is the adjective meaning in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Whaling is the hunting of whales at sea, a marine activity.

clue.text: I simpered awkwardly, showing skin

indicators.note: the letters of i simpered are placed clumsily in a new order

explanation.surface: An embarrassed smile reveals a bit too much flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of the skin.

clue.text: Fellow one's pulled from the sea

indicators.note: taken out of the word for the sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor is hauled out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A man is a fellow, a chap.

clue.text: Manage failure, letting one go

indicators.note: with go, says the letter for one is released from the word
with letting, signals dropping the letter for one

parts.note: ruin is collapse or failure
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boss handles a failing business by laying someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something is to manage or operate it.

clue.text: Plaything most of you duplicated

indicators.note: the shortened word is written twice
all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A toy that mostly reflects yourself twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spool toy that climbs and falls on a string.

clue.text: Request core part of French agreement

indicators.note: the central pair of letters of the word French is taken

parts.note: a treaty is a formal agreement between states

explanation.surface: A plea about the central clause of a French accord.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or request.
